prompt: After a control-plane canary upgrade, API latency rises, webhooks time out, controller queues grow, and tenant automation retries aggressively. Lead containment and recovery.
directAnswer: Stop the upgrade wave and declare API/control-plane impact. Bind old/new API server, controller, scheduler, etcd, admission/conversion and add-on versions; request/audit IDs; APF priority/queue/rejection data; webhook endpoint/TLS/latency/failure policy; etcd leader/commit/space alarms; controller queue age and the tenant client retry rate. Contain retry amplification and preserve critical API traffic through predesigned fairness/rate controls. Determine whether skew, new fields/versions, webhook compatibility, etcd latency or resource saturation is first. Restore the canary through the tested rollback/rebuild path or apply a bounded forward fix. Verify readyz, API write/read SLI, etcd, controllers, admission positives/negatives, workload reconciliation and user journeys before resuming any wave. Add compatibility and retry-load canaries to prevention.
foundation: An upgrade can expose a compatibility failure that retry amplification turns into control-plane overload.
seniorAnswer: I separate initiating incompatibility from overload amplification and preserve the control plane's recovery traffic before adding capacity or continuing versions.
weakAnswer: Upgrade all API servers so versions match and scale them out.
whyWeak: It spreads the unproven change and may intensify load on webhooks or etcd.

evidence.signal: stable API, reconcile and user SLI

followUps.answer: Retries may consume the exact control-plane capacity recovery requires.
Only after root cause, compatible canary, soak and every abort gate are satisfied.
